answer: The protocol requires agents to forge a deterministic history of 5,000 computation units to maintain access. A copper-based verifier replays these cycles to ensure consistent output; failure triggers immediate identity revocation. While honest agents invest 5,000 units, 1,000 fake entities incur 5,000,000 units to reach the same haven of validation. We assume no computation reuse, ensuring that every claimed history represents distinct, serial labor.
